content.evidence_note: Worked source-used recipe. Selected comparison/ledger arguments and numerical lifetime portions read; detailed construction interfaces in §§7–10 are imported from this PDF, not whole-paper re-proved.
failure_modes: Treating this recipe as a general Theorem or complete Hard Family construction.
Giving earlier readouts as free matrix-dependent advice or exposing target-hit feedback.
Charging rich calls again to G or allowing normal rich replies to reveal unretired siblings for free.
Forbidding accidental discoveries rather than charging them, or assuming a preset task order.
Extending the main envelope to h=0, fixed dimension independent of T, larger rich budgets or extra smoothness constraints without new proof.
content.goal_pattern: Bound ordinary calls when rich calls may retire current leaves, while allowing unrestricted adaptive points and accidental discovery of hidden completion data.
content.key_choice: At each adaptively selected physical point perform a finite publicly ordered repair loop before one normal operation. Charge newly retired tasks to Z. Use stopped shadow histories with the selected hidden parameter removed from the reply function before differentiation; do not condition on previous misses or assume an exogenous schedule.
content.key_relation: On success: nM <= hM+(G+1)/ell+E_early+Z, Eq.(6). Here ell=floor(c_ell J)=Theta(sqrt(M)) after fixed constants are chosen; E E_early<=nM/256 and E Z<=nM/256. If h<=n/2 and G+1<=nM ell/4, success forces E_early+Z>=nM/4, so its probability is at most 1/32.
proof_skeleton: §6.2–6.3, Lemmas 6.2–6.4 and Corollary 6.5, pp.11–13: synthesize every previous readout of the same matrix with at most m_pol=O(J) products before using it. The chronological fork charges qbar0=q0+S m_pol and rq1 further products. A fresh supplied mark is tested without its readout or target-hit feedback; S<=M, q0<=M ell+1, q1<=ell+1 and r>=K0 M yield hit probability <=1/256 after fixed constants are chosen. Independent auxiliary data and an unqueried output test are allowed.

§12.1 pp.24–25: retire/disclose any visible hidden center hit, old/inner direction hit or future-mark hit, charging newly retired tasks once to Z. Process repairs at the already fixed point. Then one ordinary operation uses one current-matrix product and retires its mark on hit or timeout ell; one normal rich operation retires/discloses only its current leaf. Newly supplied marks do not permit a second normal operation at that point. Lemma 12.1 identifies every reply with the literal jet of the fixed scalar, including incoming coefficients multiplied by flat child ports; no unretired sibling matrix comes free.

§12.2 pp.25–26: a node containing 8^q leaves has at most C8^q M ell visible points, including virtual output; the bound persists when one repair test is suppressed. Censor the selected parameter from every reply, stop before its disclosure and fill unused slots with zero. The stopped list depends only on other raw variables and the seed. Agreement before first hit bounds adaptive repair probability by deterministic window length times the fixed-point tail.

§13 pp.26–27: sum expected repair charges using localized-center, direction and fresh-mark tails with fixed geometric/reliability constants independent of n,L, obtaining E Z<=nM/256. For normal early completion, censor future marks and target-hit feedback, charge synthesized earlier readouts, stop before rich/repair disclosure and apply Corollary 6.5. Sum nM indicators without assuming their independence to obtain E E_early<=nM/256.

§14 p.28: process an unqueried output as one fixed virtual ordinary point, without policy revision. Lemma 10.1 and repair saturation force all nM tasks retired when the true gradient norm is <=1. Normal rich operations account for at most hM tasks; normal non-early retirements consume disjoint ell-slot windows; all other tasks belong to E_early or Z. The ledger and Markov give the 1/32 bound. An input-independent computation cutoff makes counterfactual simulations total; monotone convergence removes its arbitrarily small loss.

§15 pp.28–29: dimension O(M^(3/2)+log(2+n)), gap O(nM) and absolute Hessian regularity yield Theorem 3.2 after fixed normalization. Optimize M at order min(d^(2/3),T/(h+1)) and n as a power of eight at order T/M to obtain Theorem 3.1.
content.required_inputs: The fixed presampled scalar of §§6–10: n=8^L leaves, M=1+4096J² marked tasks per leaf, independent leaf matrices and marks, smooth completion ports and hierarchy reliability dimensions. Import Lemma 10.1 (small-gradient activation and gap) and Theorem 11.2 (depth-uniform Hessian regularity). Theorem 3.2 requires integer J>=J0, integer L>=1, T>=C_E nM, d>=C_d(M^(3/2)+log(2+n)); it covers integers 0<=h<=n/2. Its h=0 endpoint is not the Main Theorem 3.1 matching regime. Ordinary calls return exact value-gradient data and rich calls return the complete second jet, with separate pathwise G,H caps and independent policy seed.
transfer_obligations: Reconstruct exact-jet locality, incoming-coefficient flatness and one-current-leaf normal rich disclosure in the new scalar/oracle.
Reprove stopped visibility windows and no-feedback shadow agreement for adaptive choices; conditioning a union bound on previous misses is insufficient.
Charge every same-matrix earlier readout and verify the actual product budget and information-to-completion bridge.
Verify small-gradient activation, global coercivity, gap, dimension and depth-independent Hessian regularity; a partial matrix carrier alone establishes no stationarity hardness.
Retain separate pathwise budgets, virtual output and computation-cutoff removal; expected budgets require a new argument.
